title: Momentum Module 2 Lesson 1: Coalescence Common Velocity custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Two particles $A$ and $B$, of masses $0.4\text{ kg}$ and $0.6\text{ kg}$ respectively, move in the same direction along a straight horizontal line. Particle $A$ has speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and particle $B$ has speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Particle $A$ collides with particle $B$ and the two particles coalesce. Calculate the common speed of the combined particle immediately after the collision.

A model truck $P$ of mass $1.5\text{ kg}$ travels along a smooth horizontal track with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$. It collides with a stationary model truck $Q$ of mass $4.5\text{ kg}$. The two trucks couple together upon collision and move as a single body. Find their common speed immediately after the collision.

Particle $A$ of mass $0.8\text{ kg}$ moves to the right with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a straight horizontal track. Particle $B$ of mass $1.2\text{ kg}$ moves to the left towards $A$ with speed $2.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The particles collide and coalesce. Find the speed and direction of motion of the combined particle immediately after the collision.

Particle $X$ of mass $m\text{ kg}$ moves with speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a smooth horizontal plane and collides directly with a stationary particle $Y$ of mass $0.9\text{ kg}$. The two particles coalesce and move together with a common speed of $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the value of $m$.

Particle $P$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ moving with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ collides directly with a stationary particle $Q$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ on a smooth horizontal surface. The particles coalesce upon impact. Calculate the loss in kinetic energy caused by the collision.

Particle $A$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ moves along a smooth horizontal floor with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and collides directly with a stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$. The two particles coalesce to form a combined particle. Calculate the magnitude of the impulse exerted by $A$ on $B$ during the collision.

questions.prompt: Two railway trucks $A$ and $B$, of masses $1200\text{ kg}$ and $800\text{ kg}$ respectively, move towards each other on a straight horizontal track. Truck $A$ has speed $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and truck $B$ has speed $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The trucks collide directly and couple together upon impact.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Taking the initial direction of motion of truck $A$ as positive, find the common velocity of the coupled trucks immediately after the collision, stating their speed and direction of motion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the loss of kinetic energy caused by the collision.

questions.prompt: Two particles $P$ and $Q$ have masses $0.25\text{ kg}$ and $m\text{ kg}$ respectively. Particle $P$ moves along a smooth horizontal plane with a speed of $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards particle $Q$, which is moving directly towards $P$ with a speed of $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. When the particles collide, they coalesce to form a combined particle $C$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Given that particle $C$ comes to instantaneous rest immediately after the collision, find the value of $m$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given instead that $m = 0.25\text{ kg}$, find the speed of $C$ immediately after the collision, and state its direction of motion.

questions.prompt: Two blocks $A$ and $B$, of masses $0.8\text{ kg}$ and $1.2\text{ kg}$ respectively, lie on a rough horizontal floor. Block $B$ is initially at rest, and block $A$ is projected directly towards block $B$ with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The two blocks collide and coalesce to form a combined block $C$ of mass $2.0\text{ kg}$. The coefficient of friction between the floor and block $C$ is $\mu = 0.25$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of block $C$ immediately after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the magnitude of the frictional force acting on block $C$, and calculate the distance block $C$ travels across the floor before coming to rest.

questions.prompt: A trolley of mass $1.6\text{ kg}$ is moving in a straight line along a smooth horizontal track with a constant speed of $3.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. A small lump of clay of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ falls vertically onto the trolley and adheres (coalesces) to it.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State why horizontal linear momentum is conserved during this collision, and find the speed of the trolley with the clay immediately after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the loss in horizontal kinetic energy of the system resulting from the impact, and find the magnitude of the horizontal impulse exerted by the trolley on the clay.

questions.prompt: A particle $A$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at a point $X$ on a smooth plane inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = 0.45$. The particle slides down the plane for a distance of $4.0\text{ m}$ to a point $Y$, where it collides directly with a stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.9\text{ kg}$. Particles $A$ and $B$ coalesce at $Y$ to form a combined particle $C$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the acceleration of $A$ down the plane, and show that its speed immediately before colliding with $B$ is $6.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the common speed of $C$ immediately after the collision, and find the magnitude of the impulse exerted by $A$ on $B$ during the collision.

questions.prompt: Three particles $P$, $Q$, and $R$ lie in a straight line on a smooth horizontal table, with masses $0.5\text{ kg}$, $0.3\text{ kg}$, and $0.8\text{ kg}$ respectively. Initially, $Q$ and $R$ are stationary. Particle $P$ is projected directly towards $Q$ with speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$. When $P$ collides with $Q$, they coalesce to form a composite particle $PQ$. Particle $PQ$ then continues along the table and collides directly with $R$, coalescing with $R$ to form a composite particle $PQR$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $PQ$ immediately after the first collision, and find the speed of $PQR$ immediately after the second collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the amount of kinetic energy lost in the first collision.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the amount of kinetic energy lost in the second collision, and determine the overall percentage of the original kinetic energy that is lost across both collisions combined.

questions.prompt: A wooden block of mass $1.9\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal surface. The coefficient of friction between the block and the surface is $\mu = 0.15$. A bullet of mass $0.1\text{ kg}$ is fired horizontally into the block with unknown speed $u\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The bullet embeds itself in the block instantaneously, and the combined block and bullet slide a distance of $3.0\text{ m}$ along the surface before coming to rest. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the magnitude of the frictional force acting on the combined block and bullet, find the deceleration of the combined body, and show that its speed immediately after the bullet embeds is $3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using the principle of conservation of linear momentum, find the speed $u$ with which the bullet was fired, and calculate the mechanical energy converted into heat and sound during the embedding process.
